Memory for: SB_READ_ONLY is legacy now. What's the per-space replacement that stops all writes, including by admins, and what happens to member permissions?
[1] Install/Configuration.md (Network)
  Run mode: * `SB_READ_ONLY` *(legacy)*: If you want to run the SilverBullet client and server in read-only mode (you get the full SilverBullet client, but all edit functionality and commands are disabled), you can do this by setting this environment variable to a non-empty value. Upon the server start a full space index will happen, after which all write operations will be disabled. Prefer the per-space settings in the [[Dashboard]]: give the public read access to publish a space (see [[Publishing]]), or **Freeze this space** to stop all writes.
  Authentication: * `SB_USER` (single-space only): Sets single-user credentials, in `username:password` form. Use a long password and protect the process configuration. / * `SB_AUTH_TOKEN` (single-space only): Enables `Authorization: Bearer <token>` style authentication on the [[HTTP API]]. In multi-space mode this is replaced by per-account [[Authentication#API|API tokens]]. / * `SB_LOCKOUT_LIMIT`: Specifies the number of failed login attempt before locking the user out (for a `SB_LOCKOUT_TIME` specified amount of seconds), defaults to `10` / * `SB_LOCKOUT_TIME`: Specifies the amount of time (in seconds) a client will be blocked until attempting to log back in, defaults to `60`. / * `SB_REMEMBER_ME_HOURS`: Sets the session duration in hours when “Remember me” is checked during login, defaults to 7 days. Sessions where “Remember me” was left unchecked always last one week.
[2] CHANGELOG.md (CHANGELOG)
  2.10.0: * Fix: writing to a read-only path (anything served from the bundled library, a `SB_READ_ONLY` server) returned a 500, which clients could not tell apart from a temporary server fault — so a syncing client retried it forever. Read-only refusals now return 403, and the sync engine records the path and stops re-attempting it until the local file changes. This most often bit spaces holding a stale copy of a `Library/Std` page that a later release had dropped from the bundle. / * Fix: major typing/navigation slowdown on pages with many internal links in large spaces.
  Edge: * `sb fs write`, `sb fs edit` and `sb fs rm` take `--revision` (`--if-match` still works). Writing or editing a page with Space Lua or Space Style now reloads its scripts and reports its load errors and lint problems, and exits with code 9 ("written, but its scripts have problems") when there are any; `--no-reload` skips it. After changing files outside `sb` you still need `sb lua 'system.reboot()'`. / * `--space` accepts a space's name in any case or its id. `sb fs` and `sb help` start a stopped folder space of [[Desktop]] in the background and wait for it, up to `--timeout`. / * Dashboard widgets (`widgets.chip`, `widgets.stat`, `widgets.bars` and `widgets.grid`) have moved out of core to the optional [Dashboard library](https://github.com/silverbulletmd/silverbullet-libraries/blob/main/L ...
Exact facts:
- [1] `SB_INDEX_PAGE` *(legacy)*: Sets the default page to load, defaults to `index`. Prefer the per-space **Index page** setting in the [[Dashboard]] (**Space settings → General**).
- [2] [[Tag/data]] block keys can no longer overwrite `ref`, `tag` or `itags`, and relations from data blocks now point at the object they’re written in. A data block named after a built-in tag (` ```#task `) is no longer indexed. Lint flags it.
